chunks: I found that endurance upon them was wiser, so I was patient although there was pricking in the eye and suffocation in the throat, I saw my inheritance being plundered, until the first one went his way, and then handed it over to Ibn al-Khattab after himself.

key_terms.الْأَوَّلُ: The first one (referring to Abu Bakr)
key_terms.شَجًا: Suffocation in the throat (metaphor for grief)
key_terms.قَذًى: Pricking in the eye (metaphor for irritation)

ai.seo_question: What was Imam Ali's stance on the early caliphate and his inheritance of leadership?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) illustrates his strategic patience (sabr) during the caliphate of the first three successors, enduring the political marginalization of his rightful inheritance with the physical discomfort of a grain in his eye and a bone in his throat. This period of restraint culminated in the transfer of authority to Umar ibn al-Khattab, a delay that Shia scholarship views as a calculated preservation of unity until the time for open assertion of leadership arrived.
